30 Days of Vibe Coding | Day 26: Your First Update After Launch
Once a system goes live, does it stop changing?
After launch, a system actually changes even more, since you'll need to adjust to what users want, how the market shifts, what competitors do, and even changes in regulations.
So in the world of Vibe Coding, how do you add a new feature after launch?
That's what this post is about.
Update the spec before you touch anything

If you remember, on Day 10 we did a scope-control exercise. We deliberately threw in a line asking for budget alerts and income tracking, and the AI pulled out the "Out" list in SPEC.md and blocked the request.
So... now that the system is live, what if you actually want that feature? It's pretty simple. Whenever you start expanding requirements, stick to one big rule:
Update the rule docs first, then start building.

Never, ever change the code first. It's a really bad habit. It's easy for the docs to fall behind the code, then you can't check features against them anymore, and every update after that just piles more on top of a shaky foundation.
So what should we do now? Pretty simple. Go into Claude Code, type
to wipe the conversation (so the Context is clean), and then enter this prompt:

The interview asks the what (what to build)
Plan Mode asks the how (how to build it)

Right now we haven't even figured out what the budget looks like or how the over-budget alert should be displayed, so this isn't the time for Plan Mode. Plan Mode would just rush to lay out implementation steps for you, while the requirements aren't even lined up yet. So here you only need to switch to
, and then get ready to be grilled one question at a time.
In my case, I got grilled with at least 8 or so questions (it'll be different for everyone).
The conversation lining up the budget alert requirements
Building the feature with Plan Mode
What's next? It's pretty straightforward from here, and it's about the same as what we've done before. Just switch to
Please build the budget alert feature following the updated @SPEC.md.
The budget alert plan from Plan Mode
If the plan looks fine, let the AI build it. Once it's done, you still need to do some review. You can come up with some edge cases to check, like:
Get this month's total to exactly 1000 on purpose and set the budget to 1000. At this point, there shouldn't be an alert.
Add another $1, and it should show you're $1 over.
Refresh the page, and the budget and the alert are both still there.
Clear the budget to 0, and the alert goes away.
Reviewing the budget alert's edge cases
You can hand the edge cases above to the AI and have it use the Claude in Chrome extension to drive the screen and test them itself.
After that it gets a lot easier. Just ask the AI to push it live, since we already set up GitHub Actions auto-deployment on Day 25.
This one was a lot simpler, since most of it was already covered in earlier days. So today was mostly a review, so you know what to do when you want to add a new feature after launch.
To add a new feature after launch, update the spec before you touch anything. Never change the code first.
Use an interview-style prompt to ask the what and clarify the requirements, and only go into Plan Mode to ask the how once the requirements are lined up. Don't mix the two up.
For small features, the interview and the plan can both be small, but don't skip the acceptance criteria. Before you start building, think through a few edge cases first.
That's it for this one. See you tomorrow!
